Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

prompt:
Iteration 1/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: I assessed all 12 new discovery results with emphasis on directional meaning, clinical-scale relevance, interval uncertainty, multiplicity, and whether the comparison cells support inference. Returned estimates are already signed to each claim direction, so I converted them mentally to raw exposed-minus-comparator contrasts when interpreting the clinical threshold: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw negative exposed-minus-comparator difference, i.e., more negative dependency scores and therefore stronger dependency. Only H7 provides clear evidence for a clinically meaningful difference in the registered direction. H7 is outcome_013 by feature_065, direction -1: signed estimate +0.1169, 95% CI [+0.0823, +0.1516]. In raw terms this is approximately -0.117, meaning feature_065-exposed samples have about 0.117 lower/more negative dependency than comparator samples. With outcome_013 mean about -0.269 and feature_065 prevalence about 0.20, the comparator mean is roughly -0.246 and the exposed mean roughly -0.363. That is about a 47% stronger dependency relative to the comparator mean, with interval roughly 33%-62% stronger. The interval excludes both zero and a clinically trivial effect, and with only 12 discovery tests it remains compelling after multiplicity adjustment. I therefore accept H7 in this dataset and request independent validation because the effect is large, biologically meaningful if the label is interpretable, and worth checking against the multiplicity and opaque-label uncertainty. The other claims do not support a clinically meaningful directional association. H2 and H4 are interaction claims whose raw intervals are predominantly opposite or near zero and do not reach the registered negative clinically meaningful direction: H2 raw interaction roughly +0.056 with raw CI approximately [-0.008, +0.120], and H4 raw roughly +0.046 with raw CI approximately [-0.017, +0.108]. H5, H9, H11, and H12 are main-effect claims with point estimates near zero and raw 95% intervals excluding clinically meaningful effects in the registered direction once the comparator scale is considered. H6 and H10 are borderline only because their intervals very narrowly reach the approximate 10%-of-comparator threshold, while point estimates are tiny and statistically non-significant; I left them unresolved but deferred rather than accepting or strongly rejecting them. H1 and H3 are interactions with intervals that still include clinically meaningful ranges; H3 in particular is underpowered/uncertain because one cell is only 62 observations despite valid Welch cells, so both are unresolved and deferred. H8 remains active as an unresolved possible signal: raw estimate approximately -0.022, raw CI approximately [-0.053, +0.009], with interval lower bounds extending beyond a plausible 10% threshold for outcome_011. It is not accepted because the interval includes zero and the point estimate is modest. Overall, H7 is the only discovery robust enough to carry forward now. No causal or generalizable biomarker claim is made from this dataset; the evidence supports only a strong association within this sample for feature_065 and outcome_013, pending validation.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: Final synthesis for iteration 1: the validation result for H7 confirms the discovery effect for outcome_013 by feature_065. The validation estimate is signed to the registered negative direction: +0.1255, independent 95% interval [+0.0735, +0.1775] at the stricter validation alpha. In raw exposed-minus-comparator terms this is approximately -0.126, with an interval roughly [-0.177, -0.073]. Given outcome_013 mean approximately -0.269 and feature_065 prevalence approximately 0.20, the comparator mean is approximately -0.244 and the exposed mean approximately -0.370, corresponding to about 51% stronger dependency, with the independent interval covering roughly 30% to 73% stronger dependency. Both discovery and independent validation intervals exclude zero and exceed the 10% relative clinical-significance threshold. I therefore accept H7 as a dataset-supported association: feature_065 exposure is associated with stronger outcome_013 CRISPR dependency within this supplied dataset. I close the exact main-effect investigation because the registered claim is now validated and further repetition of the same comparison is not the most informative next step. This claim remains an association in the supplied data, not a causal claim or a confirmed generalizable biomarker claim. Negative findings are H2, H4, H5, H9, H11, and H12, whose intervals or point estimates do not support clinically meaningful effects in the registered direction. Unresolved findings include H1 and H3, where interaction intervals are too wide; H6 and H10, where point estimates are negligible though intervals narrowly touch plausible clinical scales; and H8, a borderline outcome_011 feature_037 signal that remains unresolved and lower priority. The most informative next analysis is to characterize the accepted H7 association without overfishing: I registered two subgroup-specific tests of the same feature_065-to-outcome_013 association within complementary feature_034 strata. If both strata show a negative raw association of clinically meaningful scale, this would strengthen within-dataset robustness across a common measured subgroup structure. If the strata differ substantially, the next refinement would formally test interaction or other targeted effect modification. I avoided adding new outcomes or unrelated predictors at this stage to keep follow-up focused on the validated finding.

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the registered direction. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference that is more negative, i.e. stronger dependency. I used approximate absolute comparator means and a 10% relative threshold; dependency scores are negative, so magnitude was taken as absolute. H13 and H14 both show strong, robust feature_065 associations within the complementary feature_034 strata: signed +0.106 and +0.128, corresponding to raw approx -0.106 and -0.128 stronger dependency in feature_065=1. Relative to approximate comparator means, these are roughly 40-50% stronger dependency, and both lower confidence bounds remain well above 10%, so multiplicity is unlikely to overturn them. Therefore H13 and H14 are accepted as within-dataset subgroup-specific associations and closed. H15 tests formal effect modification by feature_034; the signed interaction is -0.022, implying a raw interaction of approx +0.022, opposite the registered direction and small. The raw interval still includes clinically meaningful interaction values, so I do not accept or reject effect modification; investigation is closed because H13/H14 are similar and there is no compelling signal to pursue this exact interaction further. Cross-outcome feature_065 tests are mostly null. H16 outcome_001 and H17 outcome_006 have tiny signed estimates approx +0.009 and +0.004, raw approx -0.009 and -0.004, but their wide intervals include borderline clinically meaningful values and outcome_006 has a small mean, making relative thresholds unstable; they remain unresolved but deferred. H19 outcome_011 is opposite-trivial: signed -0.007 and the favorable upper bound corresponds to only about 7% relative dependency change, below the 10% threshold, so it is rejected for the registered direction. H18 outcome_014 is the most interesting secondary result: signed +0.032, raw approx -0.032 stronger dependency, about 37% relative to a small approximate comparator mean, but the interval includes zero and is wide because outcome_014 is dispersed and near zero on average; it is unresolved but active as a possible secondary association. H20 tests feature_054 level_001 vs level_002 for outcome_013; signed -0.013 means raw +0.013 in the opposite direction, and even the favorable upper bound is far below 10%, so it is rejected. Overall, feature_065 remains strongly associated with outcome_013 and is not clearly associated with the other tested outcomes, except possibly outcome_014. I do not request validation here because H7 was already independently validated and H13/H14 are pre-specified robustness checks of that validated association, not new independent biomarker claims. All conclusions are within-dataset associations only; no causal interpretation or generalizability is claimed. Opaque predictor labels also prevent ruling out leakage or confounding by correlated features.
